item.text:
**Bottom line:** partially pro-stability in rhetoric and monetary tactics, but overall weak. Putin backed tight monetary policy and long-run development language, yet 2024 macro conditions were still dominated by war spending, tax extraction, inflation pressure, and reduced transparency for investors.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Weak pro | Executive Order on Russia's development goals through 2030 and for the future until 2036 | President of Russia | 2024-05-07 | https://en.special.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/73986 | Sets official goals for sustainable economic and social development, higher living standards, fair competition, entrepreneurship, and private initiative. This is the clearest stated commitment to long-term investment conditions, but it is aspirational rather than proof of implementation. | 5B.3, 5B.1 |
| Weak pro | Russian central bank warns of slower drop in inflation as it holds rates at 16% | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-04-26 | https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/russian-central-bank-warns-of-slower-drop-in-inflation-as-it-holds-rates-at-16-3400396 | The central bank kept rates high and said inflation would ease only gradually, with Putin’s broader system still allowing a restrictive anti-inflation stance. This supports monetary credibility, though it also reflects underlying macro stress. | 5B.3 |
| Weak pro | Putin urges 'balanced' central bank rate decision for overheating economy | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-12-19 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/putin-says-russias-economy-is-overheating-inflation-is-worrying-3781400 | Putin publicly acknowledged overheating and worrying inflation and said he hoped for a balanced rate decision. That is evidence of some concern for macro stability, but it is reactive crisis management, not a structural safeguard. | 5B.3 |

Putin’s public call for “balance” shows he did not simply override the bank, which slightly supports monetary credibility. | 5B.3, 5B.2 |
| Against | Russian economy shows solid growth despite Ukraine war sanctions | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-28 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/russian-economy-shows-solid-growth-despite-ukraine-war-sanctions-3591756 | The economy grew and unemployment was low, but Reuters explicitly linked much of the expansion to military production. That is headline growth, not broad investment conditions or sustainable civilian prosperity. | 5B.3, 5B.1 |

That points to fiscal extraction for war rather than responsible long-term fiscal management. | 5B.3, 5B.1 |

That weakens transparency and external scrutiny, both of which matter for investor confidence and long-term investment conditions. | 5B.3, 5B.2 |
| Against | Russia: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2024 | Freedom House says corruption is pervasive and the regime distributes economic assets to allies in exchange for loyalty and protection from prosecution. That is inconsistent with durable fiscal responsibility or clean investment conditions. | 5B.3, 5B.2, 5B.1 |

**Assessment**
- The best pro evidence is limited to long-run rhetoric and a central bank that still used high rates to fight inflation.
- The stronger pattern is negative: war-financed growth, tax extraction, high inflation, and reduced transparency.
- I did not find strong evidence in 2024 of a sustained, broad macro-stability strategy that was insulated from the war economy.

**Search gap**
- I did not find credible 2024 evidence that Putin meaningfully protected long-term civilian investment conditions through predictable rules, low corruption, or fiscal restraint.
- I also did not find strong evidence that monetary institutions were free from political pressure, only that they retained enough room to keep rates restrictive.
